utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, counsel. Mark Harmon, Ann Sutherland, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Today in the courtroom, appearing on behalf of Mr. Perisic, Milos Androvic, Tina Drolec, Daniela Tasic, and Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith, and myself, Novak Lukic, as Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tesic, just to remind you -- good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind you that you're still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just before I call you, Madam Sutherland. Just to apologise for the late start. It was for reasons beyond our control. I hope we are forgiven. You may start, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tesic. On Thursday, we dealt very briefly with your military career, and you said that you were a member of the Guards Brigade for 14 years, from 1990 to 2004, and that you were appointed the Chief of Staff of the Guards Brigade in 1997, and you were Deputy Commander of that brigade between 2000 -- and the 31st of March, 2004. On Thursday, at transcript 1888 to 1889, you said that the Guards Brigade was a unit within the Special Units Corps. In December 1993, who was the commander of the Special Units Corps?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Special Units Corps in December 1993 was Colonel Miodrag Panic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Specifically in December 1993, who was Colonel Panic's superior officer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, Mr. Panic's superior was the Chief of General Staff, General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P351 on the screen. It's the organisational chart for the Special Units Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this was the document that you had produced last week. We can see in the box for the chief -- the Commander of the Special Units Corps is Colonel Panic and that his Chief of Staff is Colonel Petkovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can also see that the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade is Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, and his Chief of Staff is Miladinovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down when pronouncing the names. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We didn't get your answer on the record.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: For the 72nd Special Brigade, it says that the -- first of all, it has two names under that box. Who was the commander of the 72nd Special Brigade in December 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 72nd Special Brigade in 1993 was Lieutenant-Colonel Stupar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who was Lieutenant-Colonel Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at that time he was Chief of Staff of the 72nd Special Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with that document. Could we have Rule 65 ter number 09378 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is the organisational chart for the Guards Brigade as at December 1993, which you -- is this the chart that you had produced last Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this chart complete, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes, 90 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And when you say "for the most part," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a minor unit is omitted, but it was a long time ago, so I can't remember anymore. It was a long time ago, I said, so maybe a minor unit has been omitted, a minor unit that I don't think is very important for this schematic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender that chart into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The chart is so admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P352, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with that document, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I now wish to deal with events at the end of December 1993 relating to Bosnia. What, if any, orders did you receive at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of December 1993, we received an order; I received an order from my superior officer to get ready with the other troops and, with the other units of the Special Brigade [as interpreted], to move to Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was your superior officer who gave you the order?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superior was Lieutenant-Colonel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to interrupt. I believe there's a misinterpretation. The witness said "Guards Brigade," not Special Brigade. Just to avoid confusion, the witness said "Guards Brigade," and both the Guards Brigade and Special Brigade exist. We should not confuse them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, when I asked you what order did you receive, the transcript has that you said that you were -- received an order from your superior officer "... to get ready with the other troops and, with the other units of the Special Brigade, to move to Vogosca." Was that your answer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was your superior officer who gave you the order?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superior officer at the time was Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubisa Stojimirovic, and the Chief of Staff was Lieutenant-Colonel Miladinovic, from whom I received that order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How did you receive the order? Was it written or oral?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oral.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said that you were told to go with the Guards Brigade and other units of the Special Brigade to move to Vogosca. What was the -- were you told the substance of -- what was the substance of the order? To do what?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why we were supposed to go there was to help pull out the 72nd Special Brigade from that area, to take over the bodies of the eight dead members of that brigade, and, to the extent possible, to stabilise the part of the defence line held by the Vogosca Brigade of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who else -- who else received this order?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the units that were engaged in the execution of that task.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you be more specific in relation to the units?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose there is a written document governing the move of the units towards Vogosca. I don't have that document here with me, and I haven't seen it. But it's certain that regardless of the oral order, we would not have gone there without a written order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How many -- how many men were involved in this mission to Bosnia at the end of December 2000 -- 1993, with yourself?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 200 members of the Guards Brigade as of 31st December, 1993, were located in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But initially how many men left when you left -- when you left Belgrade, how many men went with you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 100 to 120 members of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said that you received this order from your commanding officer, Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic. Did he have authority to issue that order?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as subordinate units were concerned, he had the authority to write that order. Whether he had the right to go with the unit, I would not like to say anything because I believe I'm not qualified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What I mean is did -- did the order originate from him, or did he receive that order from his superior officer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose he received it from his superior level, and that's the Special Units Corps of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then, again, the commander of the Special Corps, would have he, then, received the order from his superior officer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This previous question seemed to me to be speculative; and now, again, the witness is asked to speculate. The Prosecutor could perhaps ask the witness how, within the normal procedure, the chain of command operates from the Special Units Corps towards the Guards Brigade. But now I believe the witness is being asked to speculate with regard to a specific order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, in the normal military chain of command, when an order is given by a commanding officer, is it the case that the order comes from above -- or what is -- tell the Court, in normal command structure, how does a commanding officer receive their orders?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander has to receive orders from the superior command. Without such an order, he cannot initiate any activities. Based on an order from the superior level, he formulates all the documents that are envisaged by the order from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So with respect to the order that you received to go into Bosnia, would have Colonel Stupar from the -- who was commander of the Special Units Corps, would have he had the authorisation to order troops into a recognised independent state?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Stupar was not commander of the 72nd Special Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Miodrag Panic. You're correct. Would Panic have had authority to send troops into a recognised independent state?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Therefore, the order sending elements of the Guards Brigade and the Special Brigade into Bosnia, who would have that order come from?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it had to come from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who is the highest-ranking officer in the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could see that from the schematic a moment ago. The Chief of General Staff at the time was General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So going back to this operation at the end of December 1993, what was your function at the time? What was the position you held?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of December 1993, I was an operations officer within the staff of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you do in preparation of the movement of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations officer was supposed to create an order based on the order of the superior command, if such orders had been received, and I said before that I don't remember whether we did receive it; and the operations officer also made preparations personally for the movement into the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is it protocol for the brigade to keep a war diary of the mission?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade is duty-bound to keep all the documents stipulated by the regulations, including the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is the purpose of a war diary?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the war diary is to record all the activities within the command and all the activities of the units within a specific area in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that would be daily operations?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Daily, hourly operations, operations minute by minute, if such are taking place in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would the diary also have in it significant events that occurred during the day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations officer is obligated to enter all activities notified to him or activities that the superior officer tells him to include.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would that also include any orders that were given during the day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And does the -- is it protocol that the war diary accurately reflects all those entries that you -- all those events that you have just told us about?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was responsible for filling in the war diary?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officers on duty at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the protocol for filling in the war diary, you said that you fill in daily -- daily events. So within this diary, there would be successive entries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On a day where perhaps nothing of significance or no event occurs, would there still be an entry for that day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information has to be entered to the effect that no particular activities are taking place and that the units were working in a planned, organised manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is the procedure in respect of noting visits from high-ranking officers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you mean. Could you clarify?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So if -- if, for example, the -- as an example, the brigade received a visit from a superior officer, would that be noted in the war diary?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was a war diary kept on the mission at the end of December 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was responsible for filling in this war diary?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We set out together, Major Paunovic, also an operations officer from the Guards Brigade, and myself, and we filled in the war diary together. I don't know about anything else because I haven't seen the diary itself for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When did the detachment leave Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of the Guards Brigade set out on the 30th December, 1993, to execute their mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recall anyone in particular seeing the detachment off, anyone -- any superior officers seeing the detachment leave Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was his position at the time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, if I'm not mistaken, he was Chief of the Ground Forces of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the marching route?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The route was Belgrade, Zvornik, Vlasenica, Han Pijesak, Semizovac, and Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where did you go upon your arrival to Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we got to Vogosca, we stopped and stayed at a hotel in Vogosca, which already housed some members of the 72nd Brigade and some superior officers from the Special Units Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recall who the superior officers of the Special Corps were that were there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago, but I think Colonel Panic was there, Lieutenant-Colonel Golic, and I'm not sure for the rest. I wouldn't be certain about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Besides the 72nd Brigade that you have mentioned, were there any other elements of the Special Units Corps already in Bosnia at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the 72nd Brigade, there was a part of the Guards Brigade and part of the forces of the Armoured Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew because I saw Major Borovcanin when we arrived. I saw him at the Hotel Park. And as for the rest, I saw them later on when touring the theatre of operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When you said you were touring the theatre of operations, where were these other units situated?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the Guards Brigade was -- and part of Armoured Brigade were located immediately above the town of Vogosca occupying the nearest hilltops, and on the road between Sarajevo and Vogosca, close to the manufacturing plant for the Volkswagen Golf motor vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And these were all VJ troops?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were members of the army, and there were also members of the Republic of Srpska brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When you say "members of the army," you're talking about the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the VJ, but also in that area there were members of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned, if I'm not mistaken, somewhere on the 30th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did the Guards Brigade report back to Belgrade; and if so, how did they do that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sent daily reports in the morning hours and in the evening hours to the operations centre of the Special Units Corps of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was it protocol for this information to be passed further up the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was there telephone communication between Vogosca and Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were communications, and I presume that they were used.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is the protocol in relation to reporting to superior officers when you're in the field?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through regular reports or through telephone communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd now like to go into closed session to deal with several documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 12 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 09065 on the screen, please. If I could have page 7 of the B/C/S and page 1 of the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, the document that we have in front of us, is this the war diary that you were referring to earlier?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the first page of the war diary that I referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You had the opportunity to review this document last week; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution's lawyer showed me this war diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you said that you and Radoje Paunovic made the entries in this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the top of the first page, we see the word "operative" crossed out and the word "war" written, handwritten. Do you know who made that notation?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, if we can go through this document, and if you can point out for the Court the entries that you made in this diary. Starting with entry number 1, tell the Court whether it was yourself or Mr. Paunovic who made the entry, if we can go through each of the pages.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1, this is the information entered by me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is that your signature at the side of the -- in column number 4?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my signature, and I also entered item number 2 as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, again, your signature at the side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could just go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Items under numbers 3 and 4 were entered by me and signed by me as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, we also see another signature in the fifth column. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signature of the Commander of the Guards Brigade, Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubisa Stojimirovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Information under number 5 and 6 were entered by me, as well as information under number 9, and I also signed those; and other information under number 7, 8, and 10 were entered by Major Paunovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's his signature in the column marked number 4?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not going to take you to every single page now. I'm going to take you to entry number 16, which is on B/C/S page number 13 and English page number 8. Now, we can see there, Mr. Tesic, that the entry for number 16 is blank.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we can go to the page before that in B/C/S and in English. At the bottom of page 15, entry number 15 is dated the 6th of January, 1994. And then if we can go over to the next page, to entry number 16, and then entry number 17 is dated the 9th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recall, when you were filling out this war diary, seeing a blank space when you wrote in the diary subsequent to this date?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember, neither did I see this blank space.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And as you testified earlier, in relation to every day, something had to be put, even if it was that nothing occurred on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please go back to page 1 of the diary, and that is page -- I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can I just find out from the

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I recognise this signature. This is Major Paunovic's signature. He's an operations officer from the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Before we go to page 1, if we can go to the previous page, entry number 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Tesic, whose signature is that next to entry number 15?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In column 4, this is Major Paunovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to B/C/S page 7 and English page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, we can see in the first entry that the detachment is moving out, and it's received its marching order. Listed there, are those the members of the other units that went with you on this mission, for example, the Traffic Police, the Military Police Armoured Personnel Carrier Platoon, the Military Police Special Purposes Platoon, the Guards Motorised Brigade Command, Communications Detachment, Reconnaissance Detachment, a part of Headquarters Administration, Engineering Detachment, the 2nd Motorised Battalion, a Mortar Battery, Medical Support, Technical Support, and the Rear Security was made up of Armoured Combat Vehicle? Is that the group of units that went to Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The marching orders under number 1 is correct, accurate, and those units departed for Vogosca on the 30th of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, you had an opportunity to review this document last week. Did you see any incorrect information that had been noted in the diary?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not notice anything in particular, apart from the content of the war diary for which I believe it was written without any additions at the time it was -- it purports to be written.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, what equipment did your unit take with you to Vogosca? When I say "your unit," the detachment that you went with. What military equipment did you take?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each member carried their own equipment and arms, weapons, from the standard issue of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what other -- what other vehicles or heavy equipment, besides personal arms, was on the mission?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wheeled vehicles, trucks, armoured personnel carrier, military police vehicles. All the other equipment could be loaded onto trucks, such as mortars. There were no other such artillery. There were vehicles of infantry, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we now turn to entry number 3, which is B/C/S page 8 and English page 3 -- 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does this detail a meeting that was -- a meeting that was had on the 1st of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Panic was present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be fair to ask the question to the witness, who was at that meeting? I believe that this is slightly leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, who was present at the meeting on the 1st of January at 800 hours?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 800 hours, the meeting was attended by commanders of the units that were engaged in the area of Vogosca from within the ranks of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And following that meeting, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting, I went on reconnaissance with a group of officers to reconnoitre the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who were the officers that went on reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officers listed in the war diary, Colonel Panic, Corps Commander; Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, Commander of the Guards Brigade; Lieutenant-Colonel Vukasinovic, Security Organ in the Guards Brigade; Major Borovcanin, Commander of the 2nd Motorised Battalion; and me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could now turn to entry number 4, which is B/C/S page 8, English page 3, so just further down the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What tasks were you -- sorry, we can see that this was a meeting on the 2nd of January. What tasks were the units given on that day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks to the units are listed in the war diary. The engineering detachment was ordered to engage in preparing the positions of the mortar battery. Then the combat group from the military police ranks were supposed to engage at the front line to destroy enemy snipers and other important targets which may appear in the area of responsibility, and part of the 2nd Battalion, with the reconnaissance detachment, should organise the defence of the Donja Josevici village with the task of reinforcing the Josevici battalion defence lines, keep readiness to provide support during attacks by Josevici battalion, and engage in repelling enemy from the direction of Ugorsko.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to entry number 5, which is directly below that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This was an entry that was also written by you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this entry related to a soldier called Milos Popovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's detailing the fact that he was injured.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know what unit he was part of?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He belonged to the 2nd Motorised Battalion of Major Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could now turn to entry number 12, which is in the B/C/S page 9, and the English page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This entry is also written by you, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it's of a meeting held at 0630 hours on the 5th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. This entry is not in my handwriting. I thought you were discussing item 11 and the five items within it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. I'm taking you to entry number 12. Is that entry -- has that entry been done by Mr. Paunovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume, but I can't see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What were you asked to do at that meeting? What were you tasked to do on the 5th of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall at this particular point in time. On the 6th, I know that I was at the positions of the 2nd Motorised Battalion in the area held by the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you were to be there with Major Cvjetinovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really say before I see a part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were you and Cvjetinovic to observe the firing of the anti-aircraft guns on the targets on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that these are anti-aircraft cannons, but the activities of those forces in the wider area of Rasnik, I was supposed to monitor their operations, their activities. I was supposed to do so with Cvjetinovic, Major Cvjetinovic. And then the last passage within this item, it is referred to observation of firing of anti-aircraft cannon on the targets on the ground, yes. In other words, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then you are to monitor establishing contacts between the Kosevo Brigade and the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, the Vogosca Brigade there, is that the VJ unit, or is that the VRS unit?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kosevo and the Vogosca Brigades belonged to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, we can see that Mr. Paunovic has put his signature to that entry, entry number 12; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can go to one more entry before the break. Is that appropriate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You go ahead, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, no, we'll wait until after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at a quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, if we can look at entry number 14, which is in the B/C/S, page 12; in the English, page 7. If we can look at the entry for the meeting -- sorry, entry number 14 down the bottom of the page. On the 5th of January, 1994, at 1700 hours, we can see that this is an order of the corps commander, in relation to paragraph 1: "Pursuant to the needs and approval of the NGS VJ, the 72nd Special Brigade shall leave the area of responsibility --"

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I just want to make sure that we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "... the 72nd Special Brigade shall leave the area of responsibility of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps at 530 hours on the 6th of January, 1994." Who is the NGS VJ?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an acronym for the Chief of General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who is the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 5th of January, 1994, it was General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, it also says there under paragraph numbered 5 that the 72nd Brigade will hand over elements of troops and materiel to the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender that document -- this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P353, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We will come back to this document in a moment, Mr. Tesic, but I would like you to look at another document, and that's Rule 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this still requires closed session, unfortunately, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- Rule 65 ter number 09067. Mr. Tesic, as you can see on the screen, this is a document dated the 5th of January, 1994. Is this the order that we just saw in the war diary at entry number 14?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. Sorry, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection. That's not the reason I'm on my feet. It's just a technical matter, Your Honours. The previous document that was admitted, in the B/C/S version, the diary of the Guards Brigade, in the 65 ter document there are seven more pages before that, if you have noticed. When the Prosecutor announced the pages, she said page 7, and those six pages in the B/C/S version are actually correspondence between OTP and the state of FRY. I suppose that these six pages do not come into evidence, so that this diary, P353, practically starts from page 7 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would agree. We actually want the war diary from page 7 of the B/C/S and page 1 of the English translation, so we do not seek to have the correspondence between the Republic of Serbia and the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I hope, Madam Registrar, you are taking note of that. Thank you so much. Now, 65 ter 09067 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P354, under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would imagine even the previous one is under seal?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Rule 65 ter number 09070, please, and if we could go to page 4 of the B/C/S and page 4 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is a document with the Hotel Park letterhead, dated the 5th of January, 1994. Is this your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is a document signed by your superior officer, Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- sent to the -- sent to the VJ Special Units Corps command operations centre. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's sent to the operations centre, personally to the Chief of Staff of the Special Units Corps of the Army of Yugoslavia, Colonel Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And does this document set out the fact that the units have worked according to plan and that the 72nd Special Brigade has handed over the area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, under seal, I guess?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence under seal. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P355, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next -- sorry, in that exhibit, P354 -- 355, if we could go to the next page, and that's B/C/S page 5 and English page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, again, a document dated the 5th of January, 1994. Is this your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, again, it's sent to the VJ Special Units Corps command for the attention of the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, does this document say that part of the 72nd Special Brigade is leaving the area of responsibility of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and returning to the original garrison?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And where is the original garrison?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Garrison Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with that document. If we could have Rule 65 ter number 09072.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A technical matter again. I suppose when the Prosecutor tendered 09070 and when it was admitted under the number given that all the ten pages of that document have been tendered. In fact, those are ten separate reports. We should be precise about this. All the documents from 9070 make up this P number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would ask that all of the ten pages are admitted. I will be taking Mr. Tesic to -- back to this exhibit later on. I simply wanted to take him to two pages at the moment, which I've done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask that each time you ask for a document to be admitted, ma'am, you specify exactly what it is you want to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, the document that's on the screen in front of -- in front of us is a document dated the 13th of January, 1994. If we could -- and it's from your commanding officer, your superior officer, again, Mr. Stojimirovic, and this is a report. Who is he sending this report to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order to the units of the Guards Brigade, that is, to commanders and commanders of independent units.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, in that -- in this order, is he -- is he advising that the elements of the Guards Motorised Brigade units have reinforced the 72nd Special Brigade and entered the formation of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps on the 17th of December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that upon the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade in Vogosca on the 31st of December, 1993, the reinforcement units left the formation of the 72nd Special Brigade and entered the formation of the Guards Motorised Brigade, and that the current numerical strength in the Guards Motorised Brigade is 210 men.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that would be pursuant to those earlier orders that we saw dated the 5th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Then the document details the unit formation and what it now comprises of, and that is a communications detachment, engineering detachment, reconnaissance detachment, military police, a military police detachment for special purposes, a tank platoon, four 120-millimetre mortar batteries, five armoured combat vehicles, a mixed anti-aircraft platoon, including two Pragas. What are Pragas?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These weapons are intended for combat against targets in the air.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It also says in paragraph 2 that: "Pursuant to the order of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps commander of 2nd of January, 1994, the Guards Motorised Brigade entered the reserve formation of the SRK ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does it then go on to say that independently of that order, "since the 2nd of January, 1994, all the Guards Motorised Brigade units, except for the military police platoon, have been engaged in the area of responsibility of the Vogosca, Mrkonjic and Kosevo Brigades," some elements having been engaged with the 72nd Special Brigade prior to that date, that is, prior to the 2nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. If we could just go back to that page. I have a question to ask. Mr. Tesic, what does it mean to say that "the Guards Motorised Brigade entered the reserve formation of the SRK"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The very term "reserve" is clear. It is the right of the commander of the unit to use the units in view of the situation as it has developed. So the unit can be brought in from the reserve and used in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: With the SRK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P356 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: While we still have the document on the screen, if we could go to page 3 of -- the second page of the document, of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, does it also -- does this document also say that: "In the next activities, the aforementioned Guards Brigade forces can be engaged along the direction of the main impact within the formation of the BG-2 or BG-3 ..."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the order says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what do you understand BG-2 or BG-3 or, in fact, BG-1 to mean?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an acronym. Combat group 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Rule 65 ter number 095 -- 075 on the screen, please. The Rule 65 ter number is 09075.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is a document dated the 15th of January, 1994. As you can see, it's from the commander Dragan Josipovic. Who is it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Dragan Josipovic was one of the commanders of the Army of Republika Srpska. This order was sent to a large number of units on brigade level in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is one of the units it's being sent to the reserve units of the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see all the addressees, so one of them is -- are the reserve units of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is an order to -- in relation to the movement of motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to object all the time to leading questions in disputable matters, but I think the Prosecutor is leading the witness too much. It would be fairer to ask the witness what we can see from the document and what it means. This is, after all, examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I take my learned friend's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would seek to tender that document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, under seal --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P357, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can move into open session at the moment, if that document is taken off the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Rule 65 ter number 01222 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is the date of this document? And who is it from and who is it to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was drafted on the 25th of December, 1993, at the Main Staff of the VRS, and it was signed by Deputy Commander Manojlo Milovanovic. Deputy Commander, Major-General Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in this document, is any reference made to the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does it say about the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the use and designation by the term "VJ," Vojska Jugoslavija, that is, Army of Yugoslavia, in regular and telephone communications is banned. Similarly, the use of any reference to the reserve of the Main Staff, that is, the reserve of the Main Staff of the VRS, is also forbidden.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I can take you to the last sentence of the paragraph. Could you read the last sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The forces of the Army of Yugoslavia should be treated as the reserve of the Main Staff of the VRS regardless of the number, size, strength, and type."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this order in line with the previous orders that we have seen?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no need --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Not under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P358, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Rule 65 ter number 01223 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is the date of this document? Who is it from and who is it to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 27th of December, 1993. It is an interim report sent to the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska and is sent by - if we could scroll down - sent by the Commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, Major-General Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is General Galic reporting on in this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He reports on the Pancir-2 operation and an attack by the combat group 1, and also reports on other elements referred to in this order, and I'd rather not mention them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does it say in relation to the operation? When was the date of the operation?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation, as stated here, was conducted on the 27th of December, 1993. It was commanded by Colonel Stupar, Commander of the 72nd Special Brigade of the VJ, against a medical centre facility. It describes when the attack began, how many members of the opposing forces were present in the facility, and describes that seven members of the 72nd Special Brigade were killed on that occasion. It also states that in other brigades there were casualties; members of those were killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the date of the operation?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 27th December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned that seven were -- seven members of the 72nd Brigade were killed. Does it further on make any reference to any members of the VJ being killed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight members were killed in total who were members of the 72nd Special Brigade during that operation, and that 72nd Brigade was from the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does it say where they were killed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, it is stated that it went for the medical centre facility under the name of Betanija.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was there also an attack on Orahov Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Yes, Madam Sutherland, you are asking leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another thing I'd like to add, Your Honour. This witness has come to testify here on things which are known to him. I believe the Prosecutor is trying too much in terms of analysis of the mentioned documents. First, maybe he should have been asked what he knew and then to be corroborated by documents. This happened before his arrival there. He's asked to relate the contents of that document. Let's ask the witness about the facts that he knew and witnessed and then discuss the facts before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness has already testified that he was ordered to go to Bosnia to retrieve eight VJ officers -- the bodies of eight VJ soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That may be so, ma'am. Then he must tell us the full story from his memory. He's a fact witness; he's not an expert witness, and for you to put exhibits before him and ask him questions which he just reads from there doesn't give us any idea on the -- on his memory of the events. I think you must put your documents on the screen once he has already testified for the document to confirm what he has already told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P359.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what specific tasks did Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic give you in regard to the retrieval of the eight bodies of the 72nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before our departure to the area of Republika Srpska, we were told that we were going to go there to retrieve the bodies, to replace the 72nd Special Brigade, and to help stabilise the front line in the area of Vogosca in the light of the casualties suffered. Upon our arrival to Vogosca, we engaged in stabilising the system of defence of the Vogosca Brigade. Part of our officers was in charge of maintaining communication and getting hold of the bodies of the killed members of the 72nd Brigade. Some of those officers received some of those bodies on the 14th of January, it seems to me, in 1994; and the last body to be received was received on the 25th or the 28th of January, 1994, when our return to Belgrade started. And by this return, I mean the return of the Guards Brigade to the home formation, home unit in Belgrade, in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were you asked -- in regard to the bodies, were you asked to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no. You're going to ask a leading question. "What were you asked?"

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to what you were tasked to do, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the intelligence and security organs, we contacted the other side, since the bodies of the killed members of the 72nd Brigade were taken and removed from the medical centre facility. Further communication went through security organs with a view of retrieving their bodies, and there was no engagement of the Guards Brigade in this task, since there was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go into closed session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 3 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 09066 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Before that comes up, Mr. Tesic, what, if any, documents were you asked to prepare?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest, in fact, that even before that document comes - don't pull it back first - ask your questions on that document, and let the document come to confirm what the witness has testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations organ keeps all the documents as required by the rule book. Which specific document you mean, I don't know, but I can explain it. I do believe that the command of the Guards Brigade maintain all the records and documents as per requirements.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What, if any, documents did you prepare in relation to the bodies that you retrieved -- that were retrieved -- or that were killed, I'm sorry, in relation to the soldiers who were killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations organ, which means the command of the Guards Brigade, keeps documents on all casualties, be it killed or wounded, in a certain action. And in this particular case I remember, since the 72nd Brigade went out of the area of the Republic of Srpska, all the data that I entered for those members and for the members of the Guards Brigade I retrieved from the medical centre, our clinic, which was located at Semizovac near Vogosca from the protocols on those killed and wounded in action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, can I understand, you retrieved your clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The names and surnames were received from their officers who were supposed to go to Belgrade, and the other information on the time and place and type of wounds were retrieved from the documents of our infirmary, which was located at Semizovac, which lies 10 kilometres away from Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did you do with --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did you do with this information?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I maintained those documents and included them among the other documents which I had to keep as per my duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What information did you include in the documentation that you kept?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had lists of killed in action - that was one document - and those wounded in action, and we maintained records in terms of names, time, place of casualty, and all the other relevant information that was available to us at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 09066 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a list of killed and missing members of the 72nd Special Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who authored this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drafted this document. This is in my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does the document state where the person was killed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We see reference there to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the document and page -- yes, both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- reference to the word "Blazuj." Am I pronouncing that correctly?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blazuj is referred to as probably the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Whereabouts is that medical centre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do we see Blazuj?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the -- column number 7, Your Honour. For the seventh entry, for example -- oh, the fifth entry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Whereabouts is Blazuj medical centre?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the vicinity of Rajlovac it is referred to, most probably because of the type of wounds that had to be treated there, and then what it refers to is VMA, or the Army Medical Academy. They were most probably transported to Belgrade. These facilities are not in the area of combat operations. This refers to the medical facility, at least in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does the acronym "VMA" stand for?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The acronym "VMA" means the Army Medical Academy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which he has just told you a few minutes ago at line 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So -- sorry, if you listen to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could that document be tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That document is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number and be kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P360, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I have Rule 65 -- sorry. Could I have Rule 65 ter number 08326, please. And, Your Honour, may we go into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we open the curtain, please. THE USHER: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a picture of one of the officers of the 72nd Special Brigade, Captain Galjak, who was killed on the 27th of December, 1993, in the wider area of Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P361, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May I have Rule 65 ter number 08319.06. Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this document that you see on the screen in front of you, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document that Popovic Milan, member of the 2nd Motorised Battalion of the Guards Brigade, he submitted to the Yugoslav Army judge advocate general's officer to enjoy some of his entitlements.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where does it say he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is handwritten that: "My wounding happened as follows: Between two trenches while I was running from one to the other, I was hit ..." the passage that is handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I wanted a sub-part of this exhibit, ERN number 0614-5558, which is 65 ter number 8913.06. 8319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland, I requested you to lead your witness before you place your corroborating documents on the screen. You just did that with one document, and now you're going back to what you've been doing all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. If we take the document off the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was the point, yes, seeing the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, do you know where Mr. Popovic was wounded?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wounded -- I'm not sure, somewhere around the 2nd of January, at a position held by the 2nd Motorised Battalion of our brigade in the hills overlooking Vogosca, the immediate hilltops above Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to Mr. Galjak, do you know where he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Galjak was killed on the occasion of the execution of the Pancir-2 operation in the area of the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Galjak -- sorry. Mr. Tesic, you mentioned that Mr. Galjak was killed on the 22nd of December, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say the 22nd but the 27th of December, of December 1993, when the action took place. But I couldn't be specific, since so much time has elapsed in between.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number -- I'm sorry. May we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you want to do with 08319.06 at this point in time? That's what you had called, and you asked that it be removed because of my comments.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would -- I would not be proceeding with that -- anymore with that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now you're asking to go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 14 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Rule 65 ter number 09073, page 2 of the B/C/S and page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess you have led the witness on what you are going to deal with in that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have already done so?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, does this document reflect when and how he was -- Mr. Galjak was killed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It confirms the date that I mentioned, the 27th of December, 1993, that he was killed on that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it under seal, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P362, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are a number of certificates in relation to this exhibit, and we would seek to tender them all into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A number of certificates in relation to this --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, in relation to different soldiers, different-named soldiers. I simply took this witness to one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can go through them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given that it goes for different persons, I don't want to expose my position regarding those persons. In light of my subsequent cross-examination, I believe that it would be proper for the Prosecutor to ask specifically, name by name, whether the witness knows any of those individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can go page by page. If we can start at page number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ma'am, why don't you ask this witness to tell you who else died in this incident before you put your certificates on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He's already showed us the document that he created, which listed the 8 members that were killed and 15 members that were wounded, and so it's my submission that he's already made us aware of those members that were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If Your Honour wishes, I can take you back to the document where he listed them. Perhaps if we can bring that up onto the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not necessary. It's not necessary. Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, you can see on page 1 - if we can go to page 1 of this document, of this exhibit - is that a person that to your knowledge was killed on the 27th of December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list that I made, under the heading "List of Members Killed," as well as the list of members injured, I took from the protocol of the medical centre of our own Guards Brigade, and there were some members of the Guards Brigade who were killed or wounded that I know personally. Others, I didn't know. This certificate was issued for the purposes of exercising certain rights and benefitting from certain entitlements, and I have no particular comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we have already seen the list of the deceased, according to what Madam Sutherland advised us. What's your position? Do you still insist on these people being shown and being testified to personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here's the thing: The document 65 ter 9073 consists of a number of certificates that are issued, I suppose, to the families of dead army members so that they can benefit from certain rights. Now, this document is issued concerning a person said to have been killed on the 12th of February, 1994.
