I understand the first document that Mr. Tesic made, a list of persons, but these certificates are issued concerning unit members relating to some other incidents that are not relevant. I believe that this document cannot be introduced through this witness because there has to be a link, as the Trial Chamber demands, between all these documents and this witness. And for the purposes of the Prosecutor, I believe the prior document was quite sufficient. Or, to be more precise, it can be admitted as an MFI, and then after my cross-examination, Your Honours will decide in which way to admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I ask you to be brief in your response and please focus on the question. The question is: To the extent that the Prosecution wants to deal with the deceased and injured who are listed in the list that was made by the witness, do you insist on those individuals being called one by one on the screen? I'm talking about the people on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning the document ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. So can this exhibit be admitted in its -- with the exception of page 4, which deals with someone being killed on another date other than the 27th of December, can all the documents within this exhibit be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Those documents, except for that person who was killed on another date, are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For clarification, Your Honours, we're still talking about 65 ter 09073, which was already given an exhibit number, P362, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. But then does that exhibit include that person who was killed on a different date? Isn't this person, Mladen Stjepanovic, not that kind of person?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He was -- no. He was killed on the 27th of December, Your Honour. It's the person on page 4 of that document I would seek not to tender -- have that, and that is Dragan Stjepanovic, as opposed to Mladen Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2, back to Mr. Galjak.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is your understanding of -- the first paragraph under the word "Certificate," what does this mean? In particular, that he was participating in a national defence operation. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's embarrassing to comment on documents written by other people. How they termed it, "got killed in national defence actions" or somehow or other, is something that I cannot explain. All we can see from this is that he was a member of a certain military postbox and that he was involved in combat. We know nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except that, according to the English translation, what I see is that he -- they say he participated in the People's Defence operation, not the National Defence operation. I don't know what the B/C/S says. I don't understand B/C/S, but that's what the translation says. Does it make better sense to you if it's the People's Defence operation and not the National Defence operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really couldn't say what the author of this document wanted to say. I can't explain his choice of words or the weight he attached to certain words like "people's" versus "national."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Listen to my question. Does the document make better sense to you if in the place of the word "national" you read "people's"? And if it doesn't make sense, just say it doesn't make sense still. That's all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my book, it's the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to be precise. In the B/C/S version, it says "Narodne Obrane," the People's Defence, and that's probably what the witness has read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we move back into open session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber move back into open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And may we have, again, Exhibit 08319.06, please, with the ERN number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you, Madam Sutherland. Could the document on the screen please be removed before we go into open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would the Rule 65 ter number 0614- --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You're asking for?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Rule 65 ter number 8319.06, but it's at ERN number 0614-5558.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, you mentioned that Milan Popovic was wounded on the 2nd of January, 1994. What is your understanding, or what does it mean by securing a state border?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every country is delimited by its own borders, so the state border is clearly defined and recognised under international regulations. I can't tell you exactly what this certificate means because I didn't write it myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned earlier, but where was Milan Popovic wounded?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Popovic was wounded on the 2nd of January, on a position held by the 2nd Motorised Battalion of the Guards Brigade just above the town of Vogosca, in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P363, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. Did you want to take the break now or in a few moments?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you going to be long with your next point?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to move into closed session, so it may be better to take the break now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take the break now and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I confirm we're in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we confirm whether we're in closed session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session at the moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we go into closed session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 12 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Exhibit P353 on the screen, please. May we go to page 12 of the Bosnian and page 8 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is an entry from the 6th of January, 1994, at 0630 hours, and it says there that all attacks should be taken with the aim of coming to the plateau Zuc-Orlic. What is the significance of the plateau Zuc?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a military point of view, it was the dominant elevation in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to entry number -- excuse me, Your Honour. If we could go to entry number 32, which is B/C/S pages 17 to 18 and English page 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, it says at 1500 -- 1700 hours: "Five soldiers and one officer, all from the 2nd Motorised Brigade, arrived from Belgrade." What was your understanding in relation to soldiers coming from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one correction first. Not 2nd Motorised Brigade but the 2nd motorised battalion. That was a battalion that was located there from mid-December until the dates indicated, and it was normal for a part of officers and troops working under contract to be replaced, and the officers decided that these troops should go to their original unit to resolve certain problems before coming back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How often was this occurring, troops coming and going?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rarely. Troops were rare because Vogosca is far from Belgrade and we had to use a roundabout route rather than the road going via Romanija mountain. We went instead via Kadinaj [phoen] village.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to entry number 33? That's B/C/S pages 18 to 19 and English page 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is an entry for the 21st of January, 1994, at 2100. Do you see an entry there at 1030 hours: "... soldiers of the 2nd Motorised Battalion that were rotated were sent to Belgrade ..."?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what's written, but it certainly does not relate to a large number of troops. Those were smaller groups of men, five to eight, perhaps even ten. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with that document for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, you earlier said that reporting went up the chain of command. Who drafted documents which were to be sent up the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, it would be operations officers. The documents were signed by the most senior officer in command there. For the brigade, it would be Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, and the documents were drafted by the operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you draft?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which documents you mean, but the documents you've shown me on the screen were drafted by me. I said it was my handwriting, and I confirmed that I had written them. Other documents must have been written by someone else. If you want to show me some other documents, I can try to indicate who exactly it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What do you recall drafting documents about?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents that I wrote were, first of all, daily reports or documents drafted perhaps on the orders of the commander of the Guards Brigade that needed to be sent to other units. Such documents would be drafted either by me or other operations officer and then distributed across units; that is, orders would come from commanders of superior units, then ensuing orders would be drafted in our unit and distributed lower down the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were documents that you drafted sent to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the documents you've shown me on the screen were sent to Belgrade addressed to the operations centre of the Special Units Corps, or, alternatively, to the chief of staff of the Guards Brigade who was there, but that was done exclusively on the orders of the Commander of the Guards Brigade, Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, who was in Vogosca, so that mutual communication existed and there were some orders that he issued to his own Chief of Staff in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Rule 65 ter number 09070 -- actually, that's Exhibit P335 -- 355, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, did you author this document, the first document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my handwriting, and the signature is that of Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that document's dated the 2nd of January, going to the Special Units Corps command for the attention of the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was sent to the command of the Special Units Corps, their operations centre, in fact. Yes, probably the Chief of Staff. That's written in parenthesis.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what was that reporting?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we said earlier, concerning the wounding of a soldier of the 2nd Motorised Battalion, this concerns soldier Popovic. It must be "Milan" instead of "Milos."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you author this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the absence of the commander, I must have been given authorisation to sign it, and it was sent to the operations centre of the Special Units Corps, again, to the chief of staff. This is just a report that certain officers had arrived and they had become part of the unit, that all activities were according to plan, and there were no losses, as indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is dated -- the previous document was dated the 4th of January. This document is dated the 3rd of January. Did you author this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my handwriting, and it was signed by the Commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic. It was addressed to the command of the Special Units Corps, the operations centre, along the same channel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what is this reporting?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same. Soldier Milos Popovic from the 2nd Motorised Battalion, that he was transferred to the Military Medical Academy. In the previous document, it was stated that he was transferred to the Blazuj medical facility. Here, it is reported that he was transferred to the VMA, and we asked for somebody from the 2nd Motorised Brigade command to visit the injured soldier. Under 2, there must have been some problems with the disbursement of payments, and this is what it deals with. Presumably, it was extorted out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can take you to the next document, also dated the 5th of January. Did you author this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drafted this document. This is my handwriting, and the signature is that of the Guards Brigade commander, addressed to the command of the Special Units Corps, to the operations centre, to the chief of staff, and the content is clearly visible here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. And this is a document that I took you to earlier in your testimony, and the next page, also, we discussed earlier in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's also dated the 5th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is also written by me, signed by Colonel Panic, Commander of the Special Units Corps, since we were in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next document, please, dated the 14th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this document authored by you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not draft this document --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- so I couldn't comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could scroll down a bit. It can't be seen. I believe that it was Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, as far as I can see, Guards Brigade Commander. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This document seems to be undated. Did you author this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did draft it. It must have been registered in our logbook. This is another document which is maintained at the office. I drafted it, and it is signed by the Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, Commander, and it's addressed to the command of the Special Units Corps, to the operations officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is in relation to Colonel Panic leaving for Belgrade and Chief of Staff Petkovic arriving in Vogosca on the 16th of January -- no, I'm sorry. It doesn't say Vogosca. It says he's arriving. Where was he arriving?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Vogosca. So the commander of the Special Units Corps left, and his replacement came here, and the dates are as indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this document authored by you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not draft this. This is not my handwriting. It is signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, Guards Brigade Commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the following document, is this document written by you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not my handwriting. The other things can be seen from the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was signed by Colonel Ljubisa Stojimirovic, Guards Brigade Commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you recognise that as his signature?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. This is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Then could we go to the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Again, is this authored by you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Signed by Colonel Ljubisa Stojimirovic, addressed to the operations centre of the Special Units Corps of the VJ on the date as indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, all the documents that we have -- we have just gone through were all sent to the VJ Special Units Corps command; is that correct? The operations centre -- the command and/or the operations centre of the Special Corps Units -- Special Units Corps.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sent to the operations centre of the Special Units Corps. Some of the documents were also sent for the information of the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that document in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, earlier you said that Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic was your commanding superior officer. What rank did he hold when the formation left Belgrade on the 30th of December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then he was lieutenant-colonel, and as you can see from the documents that later on - it jogged my memory - he then was promoted to the rank of colonel, through regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you see any paperwork in relation to his promotion when you were in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that then, neither did I see those documents. I do not remember that, and the Prosecution lawyer showed me some of those documents, and that jogged my memory, and then I stated that that was correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 09046 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, is this the document that you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Serbian language, it is a very poor copy. It is very difficult for me to assess whether this is that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be useful for the witness to see a hard copy of the document, which really is much better than this on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please show the document to Prosecution counsel before you pass it on to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you can give that back to Mr. Lukic and give this one to -- unmarked copy. Sorry, give that back to Mr. Lukic. Thank you. And show -- sorry. Mr. Usher, could you show Mr. Lukic that document before you show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is your typical order of the chief of staff -- chief of the General Staff on the promotion of officers, lieutenant-colonels, into the rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who is the -- and so who is the author of that document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the chief of the General Staff. He has his staff, personnel, who deal with promotions, drafting documents. It could be the personnel department of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Keep scrolling down, please. Let's see the end of that page in the English. Thank you. Does the document continue onto the next page?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a one-page document. It's a one-page document in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Whose name is at the bottom of the document, Mr. Tesic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bottom of the document I read now: "Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, Colonel-General Momcilo Perisic," by his own hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who is being promoted in this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By this document, from the rank of lieutenant-colonel to the infantry colonel rank, Ljubisa Stojimirovic, Commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade, is being promoted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And when is it effective from?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written here 31st of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20th of January, 1994, 20 days after this fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The translation -- sorry, the transcript says the -- oh, the 20th, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the second page of the document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document in the Serbian language has not been changed. Oh, thanks. Could you enlarge it a bit, please? This document comes from the Special Units Corps, Commander Panic Miodrag, informing officers in the field that Colonel -- Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubisa Stojimirovic has been promoted to the rank of colonel and extends his congratulations and extends best wishes for his further work.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P364.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And there's no need for that document to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And is there a need for us to still stay in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because I'm just about to go to another document that is protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Before we go to the documents, you mentioned earlier in your testimony, Mr. Tesic, that there were elements of the Guards Brigade units in Bosnia and that other units also came into Bosnia, and you mentioned a moment ago that there was some rotation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not rotation. It's replacement of troops within the ranks of the unit that was situated at Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 09068 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking at this first document, who's the author of this and where was it sent? This document is dated the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my handwriting. The author -- well, the document was signed by Colonel Panic, Commander of Special Units Corps. It is addressed to the Anti-Aircraft Defence Commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Lesanovic, and I don't see any reason to comment this content since it is self-evident.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise Mr. -- Colonel Panic's signature?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please, that is, page 3 of the English -- oh, I'm sorry. Your Honour, may I tender that document? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P365, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I please have Exhibit number 09071. And may that be under seal, please, Exhibit P365.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Exhibit P365 is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go down to the bottom of the document in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is a document dated the 10th of January, 1994. Who is the document from, and who is the document to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, it is true that it bears the date 10th of January. It can't be seen well towards the bottom, but I do believe that it was signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic. It is addressed to the Chief of Brigade Staff, Lieutenant-Colonel Miladinovic. This document deals with regular rotation of men from certain units, a total of 23 to 25 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of the document, please, the next page of this exhibit, which is another document. And this is page 3 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is a document dated the 11th of January, 1994. Who is it from, and who is it to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the handwriting. I did not draft it. The document is sent by Commander Stojimirovic to the Chief of Staff, Lieutenant-Colonel Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is this document -- is this document in relation -- what is this document in relation to as far as troops are concerned?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under item 1, it refers to the sending of some officers from the special purpose military police unit to be sent to carry out some of the tasks. Under 2, it discusses the rotation of the Praga crew. But since they were not part of our unit, I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we go to the next page of this exhibit, page 3 in the B/C/S and page 5 of the English. I'm sorry, page -- it's page 4 of the English. If we could go to the next document. I do apologise. It's on page 6 of the B/C/S and -- page 3 of the B/C/S and page 6 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, who is that document from and who is it to, and what is it relating to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, addressed to the Chief of Brigade Staff, Lieutenant-Colonel Miladinovic, and it concerns the replenishment of our troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And whereabouts -- from which unit are these troops coming from?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the composition of the Guards Brigade, the rear battalion or logistics battalion. That's under item 1, under item 2, also, and item 3, from the composition of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please. That's page 4 of the B/C/S and page 7, I think, of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's dated the 18th of January, 1994. Mr. Tesic, again, who's that document from, and who is it going to, and what is it in relation to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my handwriting. The document was signed by Commander Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic, Commander of the Guards Brigade, sent to the Chief of Brigade Staff, Lieutenant-Colonel Miladinovic, and concerns the rotation of the same group of people, in effect, but of course, it is up to you to ask questions and for me to answer. It says here that on the 18th of January it is requested for them to be sent, and on the 20th they are supposed to go back, and this specifies, also, the route they should be taking.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you remember -- we've gone over a number of documents now. Do you remember these troops being rotated in and out?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not in the sense of them being sent and not returning. There were cases where personnel would return to their units after two or three days, after they've resolved some of their issues, and there were cases of the same thing happening in the 2nd Motorised Battalion, which had the most men.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mean if they went back to Belgrade to sort out their problems, after one or two days they would then return to Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of the methods of replacement. The other would be for personnel to come from Belgrade to Vogosca and for a number of them to be sent from Vogosca to Belgrade for rest and recreation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document. There are a number of other documents -- there's a few more pages, which I can take the witness to and get him to comment whether he is familiar with the person that issued this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want the entire document tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I seek to tender the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P366.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Under seal, I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into open session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 08811 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order issued by the commander addressed to the Chief of Staff of the Special Units Corps. I wouldn't comment the content of this document because I did not draft it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This document's dated the 8th of January, 1994, and it's an order issued by the commander of the Special Units Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In there, he's ordering an officer from the 63rd Parachute Brigade to supply some rifles with laser sights; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this -- is this an order that would be in the -- included in the war diary?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be. I didn't maintain the war diary of the Guards Brigade, but this is the Special Units Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P367.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into closed session again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 20 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, you testified earlier that you -- your unit, or you and parts of your unit left on the 30th or 31st of January, 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit I was a member of set off to Vogosca on the 30th of December, 1993, from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who ordered your return to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander gave me orders, and the order to the Guards Brigade came probably from the superior command. That's the Special Units Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we have P353 on the screen again. That's the war diary. If we could go to entry number 38, which is B/C/S pages 21 and 22 and page 23 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, is this -- does this make reference to the return of the Guards Brigade, this entry of the 26th of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my handwriting. I made this entry, and the fourth item is what you asked, the beginning of our return to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have Rule 65 ter number 09074 on the screen, please. If we could go to page 3 of the English, which would be page 2 of the B/C/S. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, does that order reflect what is referred to in item 38 of the war diary? And perhaps you would like to see a --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The copy is so bad that it doesn't reflect anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you can just show it to the Defence before you give it to the witness. Sorry. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is a document dated the 26th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who's the document from, and who's it going to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, because I can't see, it should be the commander of the Special Units Corps, and the document is addressed to Colonel Petkovic, Chief of Staff of the Special Units Corps of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is this the order that is referred to in the war diary at entry number 38 in regard to pulling out of the troops?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in the first paragraph, does it say who approved the pull-out of the troops?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says who approved it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the fourth star, do you see where it says, "Pay attention to the presence of UNPROFOR"?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What do you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not comment because I didn't write this. I couldn't really say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just one moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, was there a concern in your unit as to UNPROFOR seeing VJ troops in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't feel anything of the kind. But when I was leading the column, the weather was very inclement on Mount Romanija, and I came across some of their vehicles on their way from Han Pijesak to Sokolac, and I was going in the other direction towards Belgrade, towards Serbia. I didn't notice anything, nor did we have any problems with either column.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were you --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the writer meant to say with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was it common knowledge that there were VJ troops in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I and my unit were concerned, we did not hide from anyone, and we couldn't hide even if we wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Given General Milovanovic's concern in relation to the document we looked at earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the witness is asked to speculate as to what Colonel Milovanovic meant when he was writing the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not speculating about anything. The document was quite explicit in what it said. We can bring the document back up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, your question was incomplete, so I'm not able to say whether it's speculation -- you're inviting speculation or not. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this witness was very explicit. If the Prosecutor wants things to be more precise, maybe she can ask about the particular period, line 7 -- sorry, line 15 on page 67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see. Was that what you were reacting to, Mr. Lukic? Because you stood up when the question at line 18 was being asked, first to General Milovanovic, not line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the two are directly linked. But my original objection concerned what General Milovanovic wrote in that document. The witness is asked to explain what General Milovanovic meant in this document and whether it was common knowledge, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then maybe we'll just see what the document says and take what the document says because ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If we could have Exhibit P358 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you done with this one at this stage, or are you still going to come back to it, 09074?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I wish to come back to it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is an order by Milovanovic on the 25th of December, 1993. Is he expressly stating in this document that "commanding officers and duty officers have been using the term 'Yugoslav Army' in their regular reports and telephone communications," and that "in order to protect the confidentiality and other measures of activities that we have been undertaking," he forbids the use or any reference in regular and telephone communications to the term "Yugoslav Army units"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have seen that now. What do you want from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to Milovanovic's express order not to -- well, his express order that the VJ must be kept confidential, was this -- I just put it to you: Was the presence of the VJ a secret?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What Mr. Milovanovic is writing here and using the term "Army of Yugoslavia," that relates to communication between units. But you must take into account that we belonged to someone. We have families. We have friends. We have children. All of them knew that we're there. It's difficult to hide something like that. Whether it was publicised or not, announced or not, I really couldn't say. It's very difficult to hide our presence there. It was difficult to hide the deaths of the members of the 72nd Brigade. It was talked about. It was written in the paper about. There were obituaries published. So I don't really understand the reason for this degree of confidentiality, if we all know that we had been there. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But do you agree that the presence of the VJ in Bosnia was kept a secret by both the VJ command and the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like every document has its own degree of confidentiality, in the same way every activity, every movement, has its own degree of confidentiality. It is up to the superior officer to decide on these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You knew that the JNA had to withdraw from Bosnia in May 1992, did you not?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the impression that this is cross-examination because the witness is being led to provide a certain answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're simply putting our case to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. He's your witness. You are not supposed to cross-examine him. You're supposed to get information from him. He has told you in a very lengthy answer that he does not understand why there's confidentiality because it was known that they were there. People were dying, obituaries were being made, and people were buried, and everything was happening, and he doesn't understand why this confidentiality. And you don't have a case to put to your witness. You have your witness to put your case to the Court through your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go back to 09074, if we could go to the first document, which is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tesic, we were earlier talking about the rotation of troops. This is a document dated the 23rd of January. Who is it signed by?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the bottom of the document, of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was probably signed by Colonel Branko Petkovic, Chief of Staff of the Special Units Corps. I say "probably" because I didn't often see documents signed by him, and I can't really recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And those initials that we see there, "LJS/LJS," what does that -- what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It makes me think of Ljubisa Stojimirovic, and the handwriting is also familiar, but I can't be 100 per cent sure that it's his.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in that document, is he asking for between 40 and 50 soldiers of the 63rd Parachute Brigade to be sent to Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what we can read here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in paragraph 6, does he make reference to the VJ army?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 6? No. He only mentions Colonel Petkovic, if he means the Chief of Staff of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry. If we could go to page 6 of the English translation. It's the -- it's a document dated the 28th of January, 1994. It's ERN page 0633-1151.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, who is this document by -- from, and who's it going to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the heading, we see that it was registered in military postbox 4795, written on the 28th of January, 1994. I can't see well. It's probably to all units, and it concerns the pull-out of units from Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P368, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, we can see a reference there to Pancir-2. What is your understanding of that reference there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing particular, apart from what we've read, that it's a name for that operation, that activity, whatever they called it. I wasn't involved in that, I didn't write this, and I have nothing specific to say about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that convenient?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And may Exhibit P368 be put under seal, which was the last exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And may Exhibit P368 be under seal, please. Sir, once again, just to remind you, we haven't finished with you yet. You'll have to come back tomorrow morning at 9.00. Once again, I'd remind you not to talk about the case with anybody, not even your counsel. Thank you very much. Court adjourned until 9.00 tomorrow morning, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.
